verdict.rationale: The docs say Conductor runs several agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) in parallel, and each task gets its own worktree, branch, diff and review path. When work is ready you can review the diff, then merge or archive the workspace, so you can run parallel attempts, inspect each diff and keep one. Community users confirm the worktree-based parallelism. However, nothing in the evidence describes a dedicated feature for launching several attempts at the same task or comparing their results side by side; comparing means manually switching between separate workspaces. Missing for 10: a documented multi-attempt/best-of-N launch for one task, a side-by-side comparison view across attempts, and independent hands-on evidence of the compare-and-choose workflow.
